sections.title: Playing
sections.info: How velocity becomes loudness, tone and attack. The graph shows the last key played: loudness (solid) and tone (dashed) across velocity, and a dot for each note you strike.

sections.title: Partial Arp
sections.info: Brings each note's partials forward in turn, as a melody inside the note: each swells by Boost and falls back to its natural level, overlapping the next. Off leaves the piano as measured.

paramInfo.play.touch: How hard you have to play. Light: quiet playing already reaches the loud, bright end. Heavy: you need to dig in.
paramInfo.play.dynamics: The loudness range between the softest and hardest strike. 100% is the recorded piano's own range; lower keeps soft notes louder.
paramInfo.tone.bright: Tilts every note's partials: more or less treble per octave of overtones, like harder or softer hammers.
paramInfo.tone.hammer: The strike at the start of each note: the hammer, key and soundboard's own response, as recorded from A2 up (octave bands of noise below). 0 dB is as measured.
paramInfo.string.unison: How far the two or three strings of each note are out of tune with each other: the slow beating in a sustained note, and in the treble the spread of each partial's cluster. 100% is as measured; 0% is a perfectly tuned unison.
paramInfo.string.stretch: The recorded piano's stretch tuning: low notes flatter and high notes sharper, as a tuner sets a real piano to match its stiff strings. 0% is plain equal temperament.
paramInfo.string.sustain: How long notes ring. 100% is as measured.
paramInfo.string.damper: How long the dampers take to stop a note when you let go of the key. Keys above E6 have no dampers, as on a grand (Top Dampers changes that).
paramInfo.space.width: Stereo width of the two microphones the piano was measured with.
paramInfo.space.room: A small room around the piano. The measurements are close-miked, so 0 is the dry piano.
paramInfo.tone.attack: How long each note takes to swell in at the strike. 100% is as measured for each key, from the recordings.
paramInfo.tone.body: The soundboard and room ringing on after each strike: the echo-like tail most audible on high notes. 0 dB is as measured. The key's damper stops it when you let go (above E6, where a grand has no dampers, it rings on unless Top Dampers is All keys).
paramInfo.play.tone: How much the tone darkens as you play softer. 100% is as recorded: each loudness has the tone the real piano had at that loudness. Lower keeps soft notes brighter; higher makes them darker and gentler.
paramInfo.play.softattack: How much softer notes swell in more slowly, as the hammer's felt stays on the string longer at gentle blows. 0% swells in at the measured speed whatever the velocity.
paramInfo.play.velmap: Smooth: velocity moves evenly through this piano's loudness range, with the tone that goes with each loudness. As Recorded: the sample library's own velocity layers, unevenly spaced as recorded.
paramInfo.tone.mech: The piano's mechanical sounds: each key's own noise as it comes back up and its damper lands, and the sustain pedal's thump going down and up. Measured from the recordings; 0 dB is the level the sample library mixes them at.
paramInfo.string.resonance: Sympathetic resonance: strings whose dampers are up (all of them with the sustain pedal down, and those above E6, which have none) pick up the notes you play and ring along, most where their overtones line up with the notes'. 0 dB is the default strength; −40 dB turns it off. Pressing the pedal sets the free strings ringing on its own; that follows Key & Pedal.
paramInfo.string.topdampers: A grand has no dampers above E6: those notes ring on after you let go, fading as they would held. All keys: every key is damped on release, as on many digital pianos.
paramInfo.tone.hardness: The hammer's felt. Softer dulls the partials and the strike and swells in more slowly, down to a felt-piano mute at -100%; harder brightens them and swells in faster. It moves the corner of the hammer's spectrum, measured per key and velocity from the recordings, up to three octaves either way. 0% is the recorded piano.
paramInfo.tone.strikepoint: Where along the string the hammer strikes, as a share of its length. Nearer the end (lower) is thinner and brighter; further in is darker and hollower, as the partials with a node there go quiet. The recorded piano strikes at about 12% (1/8).
paramInfo.string.stiffness: How stiff the strings are: their inharmonicity, which spreads the upper partials sharp of whole multiples of the fundamental. 0% is an ideal, harmonic string (harp-like, organ-like in the bass); 100% is the measured piano; above, stiffer, towards bells and gongs. It applies to the notes you strike next.
paramInfo.string.overtonedecay: How long the upper partials ring compared with the measured piano, the fundamental's decay kept. Below 0%, they ring on longer (bright, steely); above, they die sooner (dark, like gut or nylon strings).
paramInfo.arp.pattern: The order the partials take their turn: up the series, down, up and back, or at random (never the same twice running). Off turns the arpeggiator off: the piano as measured.
paramInfo.arp.scale: Which partials take part, by the pitch each harmonic has against the note: Major Pentatonic (harmonics 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 27…), Minor Pentatonic (with the 7th harmonic as the flat seventh), Major Triad, every harmonic, or the odd ones only (hollow, clarinet-like). The piano's stiff strings tune the upper partials a little sharp of these.
paramInfo.arp.low: The lowest partial in the pattern (1 is the fundamental). Partials below it, and above Highest, are left as they are.
paramInfo.arp.high: The highest partial in the pattern. High keys have fewer partials: the pattern uses only those the note has.
paramInfo.arp.rate: Steps per second, when Sync is off. Each note starts its pattern when it's struck.
paramInfo.arp.sync: Lock the step length to the tempo, at Division.
paramInfo.arp.division: The step length when Sync is on.
paramInfo.arp.overlap: How long each partial's swell lasts against the step. 100%: it takes two steps, so one partial rises while the last one falls. 0%: each has its step to itself, a pulse. 200%: three at once, a smear.
paramInfo.arp.boost: How far a partial rises at the top of its turn, against its natural level. Negative digs it out instead: a moving notch.
paramInfo.arp.others: Where the pattern's other partials sit while it's not their turn. 0 dB leaves them as measured; lower thins the note to the pattern, with the partials outside it (below Lowest, above Highest) carrying on as usual.
